MetricsCalculator2.mrr:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "After validating that data is a list or tuple, computes reciprocal-rank-based MRR scores, returning zero for empty input or zero total count, the first positive reciprocal-rank value for a tuple input, or the mean and per-row scores for list input." mrr]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data </REF>: tuple or list "Either a tuple (sub_list, total_num) where sub_list contains relevance scores and total_num is an integer, or a list of such tuples."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: tuple "A tuple whose first element is the computed MRR score or mean MRR score and whose second element is a list of per-element MRR values."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Check whether input data is exactly a list or exactly a tuple; if it is neither, trigger the exception flow. RESULT input_type_valid]
            [COMMAND If len(data) equals 0, return a tuple whose first element is 0.0 and second element is a single-element list containing 0.0. RESULT empty_input_early_return]
            [COMMAND If type(data) is exactly tuple, unpack data into sub_list and total_num and convert sub_list to a NumPy array. RESULT tuple_sub_list_array]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch, if total_num equals 0, return a tuple whose first element is 0.0 and second element is a single-element list containing 0.0. RESULT tuple_zero_count_early_return]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch else, compute ranking_array as 1.0 divided by the array of 1-based positions from 1 to len(sub_list). RESULT tuple_ranking_array]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch else, compute mr_np as the element-wise multiplication of sub_list and ranking_array. RESULT tuple_mr_np]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch else, initialize mr to 0.0 and iterate over mr_np in order; for each team, if team is strictly greater than 0, set mr to team and break. RESULT tuple_mr]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch else, return a tuple whose first element is mr and second element is a single-element list containing mr. RESULT tuple_return_value]
            [COMMAND If type(data) is exactly list, initialize separate_result to an empty list and start a loop over each (sub_list, total_num) in data. RESULT list_loop_started]
            [COMMAND Within the list loop, unpack the current element into sub_list and total_num and convert sub_list to a NumPy array. RESULT list_sub_list_array]
            [COMMAND Within the list loop, if total_num equals 0, set mr to 0.0. RESULT list_mr_zero_case]
            [COMMAND Within the list loop else, compute ranking_array as 1.0 divided by the array of 1-based positions from 1 to len(sub_list). RESULT list_ranking_array]
            [COMMAND Within the list loop else, compute mr_np as the element-wise multiplication of sub_list and ranking_array. RESULT list_mr_np]
            [COMMAND Within the list loop else, initialize mr to 0.0 and iterate over mr_np in order; for each team, if team is strictly greater than 0, set mr to team and break. RESULT list_mr]
            [COMMAND Within the list loop, append the computed mr to separate_result. RESULT updated_separate_result]
            [COMMAND After the list loop finishes, return a tuple whose first element is the mean of separate_result and second element is separate_result. RESULT list_return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: type(data) is not exactly list and type(data) is not exactly tuple]
        [LOG "the input must be a tuple of sub-list and total number, or an iteration of list of tuples"]
        [THROW Exception "Raised when the input data is neither a list nor a tuple."]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
MetricsCalculator2.map:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes average precision for a single relevance tuple or mean average precision over a list of relevance tuples, treating non-zero items as sequentially ranked relevant entries, weighting them by reciprocal position, and normalizing by total_num." map]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data </REF>: tuple or list "Either a tuple (sub_list, total_num) where sub_list contains relevance indicators and total_num is the normalization denominator, or a list of such tuples."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: tuple "A tuple whose first element is a float AP score for tuple input or mean AP for list input, and whose second element is the AP list: [ap] for tuple input or separate_result for list input."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Reference numpy as np for array conversion and arithmetic. RESULT np_ref]
            [COMMAND Validate that type(data) is exactly list or exactly tuple; if neither, trigger the invalid-input exception flow. RESULT type_validated]
            [COMMAND If len(data) equals 0, return the tuple (0.0, [0.0]) immediately and do not execute the subsequent type-specific flows. RESULT empty_data_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: type(data) is exactly tuple]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Unpack data into sub_list and total_num, then convert sub_list to a numpy array. RESULT tuple_sub_list_array]
            [COMMAND If total_num equals 0, return the tuple (0.0, [0.0]) immediately and skip the remaining tuple-specific non-zero steps. RESULT tuple_zero_total_result]
            [COMMAND When total_num is not zero in the tuple branch, compute ranking_array as 1.0 divided by (numpy array created from range(len(sub_list)) plus 1). RESULT tuple_ranking_array]
            [COMMAND When total_num is not zero in the tuple branch, initialize right_ranking_list as an empty list and count as 1. RESULT tuple_ranking_state]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch and non-zero total_num path, for each t in sub_list: if t equals 0, append 0 to right_ranking_list; otherwise append the current count and increment count by 1. RESULT tuple_right_ranking_list]
            [COMMAND Within the tuple branch and non-zero total_num path, compute ap as the sum of the elementwise multiplication of numpy array(right_ranking_list) and ranking_array, divided by total_num. RESULT tuple_ap]
            [COMMAND Return the tuple (ap, [ap]) from the tuple branch. RESULT tuple_branch_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: type(data) is exactly list]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize separate_result as an empty list. RESULT separate_result]
            [COMMAND For each pair (sub_list, total_num) in data, convert sub_list to a numpy array. RESULT list_sub_list_array]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over data pairs, if total_num equals 0, set ap to 0.0. RESULT list_zero_ap]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over data pairs, when total_num is not zero, compute ranking_array as 1.0 divided by (numpy array created from range(len(sub_list)) plus 1). RESULT list_ranking_array]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over data pairs and non-zero total_num path, initialize right_ranking_list as an empty list and count as 1. RESULT list_ranking_state]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over data pairs and non-zero total_num path, for each t in sub_list: if t equals 0, append 0 to right_ranking_list; otherwise append the current count and increment count by 1. RESULT list_right_ranking_list]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over data pairs and non-zero total_num path, compute ap as the sum of numpy array(right_ranking_list) multiplied by ranking_array divided by total_num. RESULT list_nonzero_ap]
            [COMMAND Append the computed ap for the current pair to separate_result. RESULT separate_result_appended]
            [COMMAND After processing all pairs in data, return the tuple (numpy.mean(separate_result), separate_result). RESULT list_branch_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: type(data) is not exactly list and type(data) is not exactly tuple]
